newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-MCNULTY WIN S.A. MASTERS A FOURTH TIME.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY WIN S.A. MASTERS A FOURTH TIME.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Mark McNulty won his fourth South African Masters title with a closing 67 at a hot, windy and humid San Lameer Country Club on Sunday.
The world number 20 fought a battle royal with halfway leader Adilson da Silva of Brazil over the front nine before stretching away from the rest of the field over the homeward loop.
With both players locked at 10-under at the turn, McNulty said his two birdies at 12 and 13 to edge a couple of strokes ahead had provided the telling blow.
"We matched each other with pars at 10 and 11 and one of us just had to make something happen. I did and a two-shot cushion at that stage makes a big difference," said McNulty.
McNulty, playing solid golf on the tight layout, finished on 276, 12-under for the tournament, while da Silva dropped two shots over his last four holes for a 70 and second place on 280.
American Bruce Vaughan, with a final round of 69, and South African Deane Pappas (72) tied for third on 286.
The day began with McNulty one shot ahead of the field but it was da Silva who made the initial running with birdies at the first two holes.
The Brazilian eventually turned in 32 with further birdies at eight and nine.
Yet he had to settle for a share of the lead as McNulty, boosted by a curling 40-foot putt for birdie at the par-four sixth, had also moved to 10-under for the tournament by the turn.
McNulty then struck the telling blow at 12 and 13.
It was his third tournament win in his last four appearances.
